Osnova has no access to the internet and collects nothing. Bookmarks, the place you stopped and the voices stay on this phone only and are not copied to the cloud or to a new phone: on a new phone, add the bookmarks again and download the voices again.

The Constitution of Ukraine of 28 June 1996 No. 254к/96-ВР, as amended up to Law No. 27-IX of 3 September 2019 (in force from 1 January 2020), word for word as published by the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine on zakon.rada.gov.ua. The English text is the official translation published by the Verkhovna Rada; in case of any difference, the Ukrainian text applies. Official documents and their official translations are not protected by copyright.\n\nThis is not a legal consultation. For an official copy, see the Verkhovna Rada\'s site.

The idea of making handy Ukrainian apps that ask for as few permissions as possible and work well offline came while I was working at my laptop in near darkness: after yet another Russian drone attack, the power was gone again. That is how Osnova began: the Constitution of Ukraine always at hand, in Ukrainian and English, even with no internet.

Osnova was made in Ukraine 🇺🇦. The Constitution is our common agreement: on the rights of every person, and on who holds power and how. Let us know our rights and duties, and read the Basic Law ourselves. This is who we are, and it is alive. We are alive.

Osnova is free software: its code is open, and anyone can check what it does. No ads, no tracking, no accounts. Freedom in software is not a small thing. It is the right to know what happens on your phone, and not to hand your life to anyone.

Yet since 2014, and since 24 February 2022 at full force, Russia has been waging war against my country. Every day, missiles and drones strike cities, homes, hospitals and power plants. The occupiers kill, abduct Ukrainian children, destroy museums, churches and libraries, and ban our language in the lands they hold. Their aim is for Ukrainians to cease to exist as a people.
We are fighting for the right to be: to live on our own land, speak our own language, create our own things. The freedom you value in software is, for us today, a matter of life.
If Osnova is useful to you, please support Ukraine. I receive none of this money: the links go straight to the organisations\' official sites.
If you are from Ukraine: thank you for being here. We hold on. We defend, we donate, we look after one another and we choose Ukrainian: together, this brings victory closer.
The links open in your browser, on the organisations\' own sites. The app knows nothing about it and receives nothing.

Each voice is downloaded once. “Download” opens the file in your browser (from GitHub or Hugging Face; those sites see the phone\'s IP address). Then “Pick the file” copies it into Osnova: only the exact voice file is accepted. Afterwards the file in Downloads can be deleted. No internet? Someone who has the voice can send you the file (“Share file”): pick it the same way.
